summary:
**AQUA·NEXUS 3D** is an interactive Earth observation prototype developed by Team Astronomicon to explore precipitation variability, environmental changes, and flood-related risks in Uruguay.

Created for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026's **“Be An Earth System Trend Detective!”**, the project combines access to NASA POWER precipitation data, interactive geographic visualizations, historical flood references, and experimental flood scenarios.

Users can explore selected river basins, examine monthly precipitation patterns, and visualize how illustrative flooding scenarios evolve over time through an interactive 3D-style map.

The platform clearly distinguishes NASA environmental data from synthetic simulations. Its 2026–2027 flood scenarios are experimental visualizations, not scientifically validated forecasts or operational early-warning predictions.

Our goal is to make Earth science more accessible while building a foundation for future long-term environmental trend detection, statistical significance testing, and integration of additional NASA satellite datasets.
details:
AQUA·NEXUS 3D — Interactive Earth System Trend Explorer

Team: Astronomicon
Challenge: Be An Earth System Trend Detective!
Study Area: Uruguay

Project Overview

AQUA·NEXUS 3D is an interactive environmental visualization prototype designed to help users explore precipitation patterns, understand flood-related risks, and investigate how Earth observation data can support environmental decision-making in Uruguay.

Our project combines interactive geographic visualization, access to NASA Earth science data, historical flood references, and experimental flood scenarios in an accessible platform.

How Does It Work?

AQUA·NEXUS 3D displays an interactive map of Uruguay with rivers, terrain features, and nine illustrative flood-risk areas.

Users can explore geographic locations, access precipitation information through NASA POWER, and visualize experimental monthly flood scenarios for 2026–2027.

The platform separates observed environmental information from simulated scenarios. Its flood visualizations are intended for exploration and communication, not as validated operational forecasts.

NASA Data and Scientific Methodology

The prototype includes access to NASA POWER precipitation data and NASA GIBS imagery services.

Our scientific development roadmap focuses on analyzing historical precipitation records to identify environmental trends, estimate rates of change, and evaluate statistical significance.

Potential future integrations include:

  • GPM IMERG: Satellite precipitation observations.
  • MERRA-2: Atmospheric reanalysis and long-term climate variability.
  • GLDAS: Land-surface hydrology and runoff-related variables.
  • SMAP: Soil moisture observations.
  • MODIS: Vegetation and land-surface changes.

Future analysis could apply linear regression and Mann-Kendall testing to investigate precipitation trends. These analyses are proposed extensions rather than completed, validated results.

Technologies Used

The prototype was developed using Python, HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with a local web server and interactive browser-based visualizations.

GitHub is used to share the project source code and documentation.

Innovation and Creativity

AQUA·NEXUS 3D brings together environmental data access, geographic exploration, and visual flood scenarios in a single interactive experience focused on Uruguay.

Instead of presenting environmental information only through technical tables, the platform uses maps, visual indicators, and a time-based simulation interface to make complex concepts easier to explore.

Intended Impact

The project aims to support environmental education, public awareness, and future scientific investigation of precipitation variability and flood-related vulnerability.

With further development, it could help students, researchers, and local communities explore environmental changes and communicate findings more effectively.

Limitations and Future Development

AQUA·NEXUS 3D is an experimental prototype. The 2026–2027 flood scenarios are illustrative and have not been scientifically validated as flood forecasts.

Future work will focus on historical trend analysis, statistical validation, additional NASA Earth observation datasets, and comparisons with documented flood events.

Our long-term goal is to transform AQUA·NEXUS 3D into a more rigorous, data-driven platform for exploring environmental change in Uruguay.
